lessons: Victim of Night was my pack 1 first pick, then I built red-white and never played it; take removal only in colours you will play, as the guide warns.
Smite the Monstrous hits only power 4+, so my two copies were dead against small fliers like Delver of Secrets and Stitched Drake; the guide's 'hold Smite for fliers' is wrong.
The WU beat me 2-1 with three Delver, Claustrophobia and Sensory Deprivation; my flier answers were Rebuke, Rolling Temblor and Into the Maw, so take a third over ground filler like Silverchase Fox.
Think Twice (taken at P1p10 and P2p6) and Dissipate were filler I cut anyway; take a playable 2-3 drop creature over these marginal blue spells.
Keep taking cheap instant removal like Victim of Night early, but my 41- and 36-turn losses to WR show the deck needed faster evasive pressure, like Vampire Interloper, sooner.
I drafted without a guide, so nothing here contradicted one; expect Galvanic Juggernaut and Moon Heron to be contested, since UG seat 3 ran both.
Traveler's Amulet took three of my picks (P1p11, P2p13, P3p12) and none made the WR deck; take playable creatures or removal over these dead picks in any colour pair.
The guide says fliers win and WU spirits lead; tonight WU seat 7 went 3-0 while my WR deck had only one flier, Voiceless Spirit, so prioritise Chapel Geist and Stitched Drake over Thraben Purebloods.
Both losses came to blue decks with Moon Heron, Stitched Drake and Spectral Flight, so save Rebuke and Brimstone Volley for fliers, not ground attackers.
Expect Smite the Monstrous: the white deck that met me in round 2 ran two copies, and they answer power-4-plus creatures like my 5-power Galvanic Juggernaut, so don't rely on one big threat.
Claustrophobia and Sensory Deprivation were my cheap answers to big threats, so take cheap pacifism-style auras like these early over marginal creatures.
I took three Ranger's Guile late and still had extra copies to cut, so spend late picks on creatures or removal instead of fight tricks.
RG had one real red removal spell, Harvest Pyre, and lost 1-2 to WU's fliers in 20 to 21 turn games; take Brimstone Volley-style removal over extra red bodies.
Tonight contradicted the guide: RG, listed as the best pair at 56%, went 1-2 in matches and 3-5 in games, so treat that rate as a small-sample hypothesis.
Dead Weight, Infernal Plunge and two Altar's Reap went unplayed in RG; once red is set by mid pack 2, take red fliers or removal over black picks.
Keep Spare from Evil in the main and cut a land: my 17-land WB deck stalled into 40- and 29-turn losses with too little late card advantage.
Plan for WR's two Rebukes and Fiend Hunter by holding back threats; my ground creatures like Unruly Mob ran out of pressure in the 40-turn game.
RG brought in Purify the Grave for game 3 against my graveyard-dependent cards, so avoid building around recursion alone unless you have a second plan.
Fliers win, as the guide says: our ground-bound BR aggro lost 1-2 and 0-2 to WU and WB decks with Stitched Drake and Screeching Bat; I took Abbey Griffin but cut it.
Bloodcrazed Neonate is poor, as the guide says; I still ran two in a deck short of evasion. Cut them for any playable flier or removal spell.
The guide says 16 lands for low-curve aggro, but I ran 17 (8 Swamp, 9 Mountain) with a cheap curve; cut one land for a two-drop.
Take removal early and build blue-white around it: Claustrophobia, Fiend Hunter, Grasp of Phantoms and Sensory Deprivation answered the threats that decided the 6-3 game record.
Round 3's games ran 46 and 47 turns, so value evasive threats like Stitched Drake and Delver of Secrets over Dissipate, Lost in the Mist and filler.
Three Delver of Secrets plus Snapcaster Mage gave this deck cheap tempo, so take extra cheap blue threats over Intangible Virtue, which I cut.
